correctness.rationale: Partial fractions and Fourier transform give four geometric-series terms for the Zak kernel B(z,r); elimination in the upper/lower torus halves and factored boundary cases yield exactly three zeros (0,0),(1/2,0),(0,1/2). Zak-Parseval reduces the lower frame bound to min(|Zg(x,omega)|²+|Zg(x,omega-delta)|²), which is zero only when the two zeros share x at delta=1/2. At this offset the spatial and frequency linear Taylor directions are orthogonal; local minimization of c0 u²+ch(u-1)² yields c0*ch/(c0+ch), while compactness/nondegeneracy control global minimizers. Independently calculated the exact c0/ch coefficient numerically (0.269312334496...) and optimized actual two-coset symbol near delta=.5 for epsilon=.01,.003,.001; all checks passed. Full infinite frame claim rests on algebraic zero classification and compactness, not sampled grid.
